techniques.name: A learned critic's accuracy is a distribution: SFT before ASPIRE showed no reliable effect over three seeds
techniques.claim: With 32 training prompts, ASPIRE's learned critic varied more between seeds than between treatments: SFT on teacher answers before ASPIRE gave no reliable change in critic accuracy (mean drops 0.06 composite, 0.008 local, under the pre-registered 0.10), while one control critic ranged from 0.425 to 0.866.
techniques.summary: aspire-si, 2026-10-07. Qwen2.5-1.5B student, LoRA r16, critic head on the last hidden layer; teachers Qwen2.5-32B (local) or Qwen + Gemma-4-31B (composite); 32 training prompts; judged on 127 pairs of a strong answer and the same answer with one planted error (pairwise accuracy, ties as half). Seed 42 alone showed control 0.866 [0.787, 0.929] against SFT-then-ASPIRE 0.646 [0.559, 0.732]. Over seeds 42/43/44 the means were 0.698 vs 0.638 (composite) and 0.635 vs 0.627 (local), so under the pre-registered three-seed rule there is no reliable difference. Critic training loss did not predict accuracy: seed 44's best critic (0.764) had loss rising from 0.91 to 1.10. The drift result did replicate: the fine-tune's representation drift points the same way on every seed (cosine 0.98, size 20.2 to 22.8), and ASPIRE's drift opposes it in all six SFT-then-ASPIRE runs (cosine -0.49 to -0.77) and in control ASPIRE too (-0.57 to -0.75), aligning with ASPIRE-after-SFT (+0.67 to +0.81). The SFT itself improved held-out answers by +0.109 [+0.016, +0.203], under its pre-registered 0.2 bar.
techniques.design_implication: Budget at least three seeds per arm for any learned critic at this scale and pre-register the decision rule; never pick a critic by its training loss; don't avoid SFT-then-preference training on the strength of one run. The drift opposition is the durable lead.
techniques.variance_note: Composite control critic 0.425 to 0.866 across seeds; local control 0.543 to 0.724. A later aspire-si test showed critic initialisation alone can invert a critic, so the 0.425 draw may be an inverted one.
techniques.measured_conditions: aspire-si runs on 2026-10-07; 32 training prompts; 127 planted-error judge pairs on 64 held-out questions.

techniques.name: Score an LLM judge in both answer orders: Qwen2.5-32B's position bias, measured on planted errors
techniques.claim: Read as a single A/B text choice, Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct picked A on all 127 pairs when the strong answer was A and the strong answer only 49/127 times when it was B. Read from its A/B log-probabilities averaged over both orders, the same model (Q4) favoured the strong answer 0.886 on 149 fresh pairs (single choice 0.685) and 0.898 on the 127 (single choice 0.701).
techniques.summary: aspire-si, 2026-10-07 and 2026-10-08. 127 judge-set pairs and 149 fresh confirmation pairs, each a strong answer and a copy with one planted error. Whole-number 0-10 absolute scores tied 89 of 127 pairs; when they separated a pair they were right 31 of 38 times. Single A/B text choices show total position bias in one order. Averaging the option probabilities over both orders recovers a real preference: Qwen2.5-32B Q4 0.886 (132/149, CI [0.823, 0.939]) on fresh pairs and 0.898 (114/127, CI [0.835, 0.952]) on the judge set, against 0.685 and 0.701 for single choices. Planting errors works when the model returns a JSON {original sentence, edited sentence} that code applies; asked to copy an answer with one change, it returned the answer unchanged 84 of 128 times.
techniques.design_implication: Every LLM judge in the studio scores both orders and averages the option probabilities; prefer forced choice to absolute scores; plant controlled defects by structured edits applied in code, never by asking a model to rewrite.
techniques.measured_conditions: aspire-si judge measurement 2026-10-07 (Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct, temperature 0) and the Kev confirmation run 2026-10-08 (Qwen2.5-32B Q4, order-averaged log-probabilities).
